c.tagline: Iran's holiest city, drawing millions to the golden shrine of Imam Reza.

taxi.fareNote: Use the Snapp or Tapsi apps for fair fixed fares. Foreign bank cards don't work in Iran, so carry cash (rials); app wallets are topped up with cash. Agree a price before boarding street or shared taxis.

emergency.note: Fire: 125. English-speaking operators are not guaranteed; hotel staff can assist.

avoid.reason: Dense crowds around the Imam Reza shrine and Bazar-e Reza attract pickpockets; keep valuables secured.

hood_desc: The pedestrianized precinct immediately around the vast Imam Reza shrine complex, with Goharshad Mosque, the Reza Bazaar and Nader Shah's tomb steps away; where most pilgrims base themselves to be within walking distance of the haram.
The busy commercial artery running from the shrine, packed with hotels, shopping arcades, saffron and souvenir shops and restaurants; convenient and lively, ideal for first-time visitors.
Older lanes northwest of the shrine along Nawab Safavi and Tabarsi streets, dense with budget guesthouses, pilgrim eateries and local markets; authentic and inexpensive.
Mashhad's upscale modern district along tree-lined Sajjad Boulevard, known for its smart restaurants, cafes and boutiques; a change of pace from the shrine crowds for dining out.
A greener residential area around Koohsangi Park stretching toward Vakilabad, with parks, quieter hotels and family homes away from the pilgrim bustle.

water.note: Tap water is chlorinated and generally safe, though many visitors prefer bottled.

transit.pay: Fares use a rechargeable Man-Card (Mashhad transit smart card) tapped at metro gates and on buses; single tickets are sold at metro stations. Foreign bank cards don't work in Iran, so top the card up with cash.
transit.hours: Metro and buses run roughly 06:00-22:00; there is no overnight service, so late-night travelers rely on Snapp or Tapsi.
transit.note: The Metro links the airport and the shrine area; the streets immediately around the Imam Reza shrine are pedestrianized and best explored on foot.

train: Mashhad Railway Station - domestic services to Tehran, Isfahan, Yazd and other cities
bus: Mashhad Central Bus Terminal (Imam Reza Terminal) - intercity coaches across Iran

transit.m: Mashhad Metro / airport bus toward the shrine area (30-40 min)
Snapp / Tapsi to the shrine area (20-30 min)

tip.r: Rounding up is appreciated in taxis and restaurants; upscale venues may add a service charge. Not deeply ingrained but increasingly common in tourist-facing places.
